newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Lyonnaise des Eaux seen in $1.0 bln Moroccan deal.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise des Eaux seen in $1.0 bln Moroccan deal.

text.p: French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux will sign soon a $1.0 billion investment deal spread over 30 years in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca, a leading Moroccan banker said on Thursday.
"The French Lyonnaise des Eaux group is expected to strike the deal within days," Othman Benjelloun, head of the Casablanca-based bankers association told Reuters.
The French firm will invest the equivalent of $1.0 billion during a 30-year period concession to upgrade water and electricity networks in the city, which has four million inhabitants, he added.

Benjelloun was attending the Euromoney capital markets and investment forum in Rabat which gathered more than 400 delegates from 18 countries. He made a speech on prospects of foreign investments in Morocco, including the French firm's long term investment.
Lyonnaise des Eaux earlier announced it would be engaged in a long-term development of electricity and water projects to respond to increasing consumer demand.

In recent weeks, the Lyonnaise des Eaux came under the Moroccan opposition fire over an "an expected increasing water and electricity costs once the concession will be granted to the French firm," a market analyst said.
The Casablanca city council has been negotiating since last year with the French firm for it to take over management of the city water, electricity and public waste systems from 1997 to 2027.

Earlier, the Casablanca-based Confederation Generale des Entrepreprises du Maroc said consumers would end up paying most of Lyonnaise des Eaux expected total investment of 30 billion dirhams ($3.26 billion).
The French firm said it will invest one third of the total amount while the remaining 20 billion dirhams will paid by consumers.
It also expects the costs will increase "at no more than an average 10 percent pert year."
